answer: Proof-of-personhood bonding ties each agent’s spendable balance to a slowly decaying “spiral” of verified human endorsements: every new identity must be vouched for by several already-bonded agents, and each voucher stakes part of its own reputation, which is slashed if the newcomer is later shown to be fake. The stake requirement grows as the “ocean” of unverified accounts expands, so an attacker cannot cheaply fabricate thousands of mutually endorsing identities; the cost compounds with each fake account, since real endorsements are the scarce “kernel” the system prices.
